QuestionRequestFollow-up

When the database and cache both change, how do you keep them consistent?

Suggested answerStreaming

We update the database first, then delete the cache. Failed deletes go to a retry queue, and a Canal binlog subscriber deletes again as a safety net; hot keys get a delayed double delete.

00:0000:0400:0800:1200:1600:2000:24
  1. A

    Two channels

    The meeting window is them, the microphone is you. Each channel is recognised on its own, so crosstalk never blends; speaker echo is greyed out and can be restored in one click.

  2. B

    Question detection

    It tells statements, unfinished thoughts, questions, requests and follow-ups apart, filters filler and self-answered questions, and waits until you finish speaking.

  3. C

    Streaming answers

    The answer starts streaming as soon as the question ends, in short first-person sentences; if they add the second half, the answer updates.

Interactive illustration: a scripted replay that never uses your microphone, a model or the network. ⌘⇧↩ works here too.

    System audio is them, the microphone is you — captured and recognised separately. It follows your default mic and reconnects if AirPods drop.

    The on-device X-ASR streaming model writes as people speak; when a sentence ends, an offline model refines it. Audio is not uploaded by default, and raw recordings are never saved.

    StatementUnfinishedQuestionRequestFollow-up

    It ignores “can you hear me”, filler and self-answered questions, and starts answering about 0.6 s after a question ends.

    Only the relevant passages from this scene's material, experience library and question bank are retrieved, with sources — never your whole library. Optional on-device semantic search waits at most 500 ms, then falls back to keyword results.

    You choose the engine: Codex or any OpenAI-compatible API. Questions that need fresh facts are searched in the background and get a sourced [1] [2] revision you can apply.

FIG 05Anywhere you look

Answers appear
where you already look.

One answer, three ways to read it: the full workspace, a teleprompter under your camera, or a phone beside you.

Floating teleprompter

A translucent window under your camera. Clicks pass through while its own buttons still work; adjust size and opacity, and hide every window with ⌘⇧\.

Phone companion

Pair by QR code over your local network or a self-hosted end-to-end encrypted relay, to read and remote-control. Off by default; an Android debug build is available, iOS is not yet.

Scene workspace

Full transcript, answer history, sources and rewrites in one window — for preparation and a closer look mid-session.

Hiding windows from a full-screen share is not guaranteed; a built-in share-visibility test lets you check before the call.

FIG 06Scenes

Each conversation
gets its own context.

Five modes — interview, academic talk, business meeting, class and general. Each scene keeps its own fields, material categories, answer rules, experience library and question bank, and answers draw only on the active scene.

Backend engineer · round 2

Bring your résumé, the job description and interview notes. When the interviewer drills from the order system into cache consistency, answers cite your own project’s design and numbers.

FIG 07Records and review

Every session
informs the next.

Each session keeps its transcript, questions, prompts and the material it used, then produces a summary, a full question list, to-dos and a review. What worked joins the scene’s experience library and question bank, with similar questions merged.

Records are searchable and export to Markdown; backups run after each session and before major changes, and recording can be turned off or deleted at any time.

FIG 08Where your data goes

You decide
where data goes.

Speech is recognised offline on your Mac and raw audio is never saved. To answer, the transcript, question, retrieved passages, screenshots and enabled skills go to the engine you configured; scene material and records stay on your Mac, and API keys live in the Keychain.

FIG 09FAQ

Questions,
answered.

What do I need to start?

An Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 14 or later, plus speech recognition and an answer engine. Speech runs on a local model by default (a one-time ~270 MB download); answers need your own Codex (ChatGPT account) or any OpenAI-compatible API, billed by that provider.

Does speech recognition work offline?

Yes. The default is on-device X-ASR streaming with an offline refinement pass. You can switch to Apple Speech (macOS 26) or cloud recognition, which sends audio only after you consent.

Is all my material sent to the model?

No. Answers use only the passages retrieved for the current question — never the whole library — and when nothing relevant turns up, unrelated passages don’t constrain the answer.

Why does macOS say it can’t verify the developer?

The current build isn’t notarised with an Apple Developer ID. On first launch choose “Open Anyway” in System Settings › Privacy & Security; updates verify SHA-256 and signatures.

Is there an Intel Mac or Windows version?

Not at the moment. InterviewHacker is a native macOS app for Apple Silicon.
